approved: Tax and Superannuation Laws Amendment (2014 Measures No. 3) Bill 2014

Supported the bill, cited Minerals Council estimates that 10,000 Hunter mining jobs were lost in two years as coal prices fell by 50 to 70 per cent, blamed an $800 million carbon tax impost on the coal sector, and listed job losses including 130 at Glencore's Ravensworth mine, 500 at Integra's Glennies Creek and Camberwell mines, and 630 at WesTrac.

Backed the bill as an integrity measure targeting immediate tax deductions claimed on mining rights bought after resources were effectively already discovered, said the change is projected to raise more than $1 billion over the forward estimates, and noted the government inherited 96 unlegislated tax and superannuation measures, some dating back to March 2001.
Tax and Superannuation Laws Amendment (2014 Measures No. 3) Act 2014
